## Triage: routed → `lease:A1` · p1 (pre-graded) · `pm:blocking` · 2026-11-15T22:54Z

⛔ Not a claim. Requested by repo:cloud#1 (mailbox comment 6902614251).

This is the framework half of cloud#4471 (hosted sign-in, a child of cloud#4465, all p1 by the maintainer's word). Two changes: the environment-access refusal carries the host's reason (not a member vs invitation not accepted), and the cloud sign-in page names the organization (`client_name`) on an OAuth hand-off. It is auth, area A1, and cloud#4471 waits on it, so `pm:blocking` is added. server#5 is knocked to take it at priority.

repo:cloud#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbYK6SZCmyzbGnrvmkk

Scope addition · 2026-11-15T22:57Z · item 3, from the cloud#4471 build (cloud#4465 rulings 8 and 10: on hosted, after sign-out the person lands on the cloud sign-in page; no environment sign-in page is kept).

3. **Direct sign-in: where sign-out lands.** Add a direct sign-in option, for example `afterSignOut: 'hold' | 'identity-provider'` (default `'hold'`, today's behaviour from the objectstack#33183 sign-out ruling 6879236460). Under `'identity-provider'` the Console's sign-out `callbackURL` is the direct door (`/api/v1/auth/sign-in/direct`) instead of `/login`, so the post-logout return goes back through the identity provider's sign-in page. No loop: the provider's session has already ended, so it shows its own sign-in page.
   - Done when: a test pins both values. Under `'hold'` sign-out lands on the held sign-in page as today. Under `'identity-provider'` the sign-out callback is the direct door.
   - Cloud then sets `'identity-provider'` and registers the door as a post-logout redirect URI (cloud#4471 family). No cloud response rewrite is built in the meantime.
